record.context_brief: Almost-inside paths in connected compact sets
record.original_question: Let K be a compact connected subset of R^n, and let p and q be points of K. For every epsilon > 0, does there exist a curve gamma connecting p to q such that the total length of the part of gamma lying outside K is less than epsilon?

evidence.quote: Let p and q be a pair of points in a compact connected subset K ⊂ R^n. Is it possible to connect p to q by a curve γ such that the length of γ \ K is arbitrarily small?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $n\geq 2$ and let $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a compact connected set. Let $p,q\in K$. Is it true that for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists a rectifiable curve $\gamma:[0,1]\to\mathbb{R}^n$ with $\gamma(0)=p$ and $\gamma(1)=q$ such that the one-dimensional Hausdorff measure (length) of the part of $\gamma$ lying outside $K$, namely $\mathcal{H}^1(\gamma([0,1])\setminus K)$, is less than $\varepsilon$?
artifact.category_tag: Connectedness and rectifiable curves in Euclidean space
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in a recent (October 2025) gallery of open problems in geometry, listed as a puzzle the author finds unresolved. No solution was located in the search.

status_evidence.title: A gallery of open problems in geometry that keep me puzzled and amused
status_evidence.snippet: Collection of open geometry problems including the question of connecting two points in a compact connected subset of R^n by a curve whose part outside K has arbitrarily small length.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is presented as an open problem in a 2025 gallery of open geometry problems.
